annotations.title: Check out a formation order in USDC

description: Creates the founder's formation order and a USDC (Solana) payment request — no API key, no Corpus sign-in. Payment is USDC on Solana ONLY. The first call takes the complete draft, the founder's contactEmail, an idempotencyKey (the same order is returned on retry), and consent { version, registeredAgentAcknowledgements: true }, which records that the founder accepted the registered-agent acknowledgements. A queue-lane order first returns a submission promise, accepted with a second call { orderId, trackingToken, acceptPromise: { termDays } }. The payment response includes a payPageUrl: an ordinary https link to a Corpus page with a QR code to scan with a phone camera, a button that opens a Solana wallet, and the address and exact amount for a manual send. The founder pays the exact amount from a self-custody wallet (never an exchange withdrawal; refunds go only to the sending wallet) and must click the confirmation link Corpus emails within 48 hours, or the order is refunded. Nothing is filed before that confirmation, and then Corpus's human review, unless the founder chose to skip review on an expedited order (offered only where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line). The tax-ID add-on is not sold here. Free; does not consume credits.

acceptPromise.description: Second call, queue lane only: the founder accepted the submission promise with this many days.

consent.description: First call: the founder's attestation to the registered-agent acknowledgements, read to them verbatim. `version` is the consentVersion formation.requirements shows.

version.description: The consentVersion of the acknowledgement text the founder accepted.

contactEmail.description: First call: the founder's email. The confirmation link is sent here; nothing files until they click it.

draft.description: First call: the complete formation draft, the same shape formation.handoff takes.

businessActivity.description: In one plain sentence, what the business actually does, in the founder's words (not the company name). Corpus researches the licenses and permits that apply from this.

ein.description: Optional EIN (federal tax ID) add-on, when available — formation.requirements states whether it can currently be sold and at what price. `wanted` records the founder's decision. No Social Security Number is accepted here: the founder enters it in a secure panel on corpuslaw.us.

hasEmployees.description: W-2 employees expected in the next 12 months.

principalActivity.description: Principal business activity in a few plain words.

expedite.description: Optional expedited state filing, available only in states where formation.requirements lists an EXPEDITE line (the price and listed days are in that line). true records that the founder chose it.

expediteSkipReview.description: Optional, with expedite: true, where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line. true records that the founder heard that SKIP REVIEW sentence verbatim and explicitly agreed. It takes effect only on an order an agent pays for directly, where the founder's email confirmation page shows the choice again before anything is filed. A handoff link ignores it: on the page the founder ticks it themselves.

naicsCode.description: NAICS industry code, 2–6 digits (formation.lookup_naics returns candidates).

parties.description: The people. LLC: at least one 'member' and an 'organizer' (one person holding both roles appears as two entries). Nonprofit: an 'incorporator' and at least 3 'director' entries (plus officers where the state requires them).

principalOffice.description: Principal office address (street, city, state required for a complete draft).

stateSpecificAnswers.description: Per-state quirk answers under the EXACT keys shown by formation.requirements (e.g. "would_you_like_to_list_members_managers_on_the_state_record"). Values are strings or booleans.

idempotencyKey.description: A random id, one per order and reused on every retry; the same key returns the same order for 24 hours.

orderId.description: Second call (or to refresh an expired charge): the orderId returned earlier.

trackingToken.description: Second call: the trackingToken returned with the orderId.

name: formation.checkout

isError.description: True when the tool could not complete successfully.

text.description: Human-readable tool result (also mirrored in content[].text).
